1) NTproBNP screening at 30 weeks is not useful in identifying infants who are at risk of developing ROP, 2) The incidence of RROP is low in infants born at ≥30 weeks, and 3) The incidence of severe ROP is also very low in infants born ≥30 weeks.

urinary NTpro‐ BNP is a promising screening tool in infants <30 weeks gestation.
there is no evidence for or against the effectiveness of the use of urinary NTproBNPt for the screening of ROP in infants >30 weeks of gestational age.
there are no data to support or refute the use of urinary NTproBNp as a screening test to identify infants at high risk of developing ROP at ≥30 weeks gestation.

urinary NTproBNPt is a useful screening tool for ROP in infants <30weeks of gestation and may be useful for ROP screening in infants >30weeks of gestational age.
